newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's housing recovery still patchy - industry.
newsitem.headline: Australia's housing recovery still patchy - industry.

text.p: Australia's housing recovery was patchy but still on track as housing affordibility stood at a record high and industry activity was forecast to strengthen through 1997, industry groups said on Thursday.

Figures released earlier showed that dwelling unit building approvals fell a seasonally-adjusted 1.8 percent in March to 11,368 from 11,578 in February, whiee the number of approvals for private sector housing rose by 4.1 percent to 7,448 in March compared with the previous month.
The Real Estate Institute of Australia cautioned that demand for housing was still weak in many areas.

Demand for residential properties in inner city areas was strong while house prices in some outer suburban and rural areas was falling in real terms, Institute president Don Brindley said in a statement.
Master Builders Australia said the fall in approvals was disappointing and confirmed that the housing recovery was patchy.

"While there has been some improvement in home buyers confidence, there still remains considerable uncertainty," Master Builders national director of economics and housing Whilhelm Harnisch said in a statement.

"Apart from home buyers confidence, all the conditions are in place for a stronger housing recovery - competitive home loan packages, high housing affordability as well as competitive house and land packages," he said.
